text.p: 3Com Corp. said Thursday its fiscal second quarter profit from operations rose a better-than-expected 71 percent on strong sales of its computer networking gear.

The company, based in Santa Clara, Calif., said profits before acquisition charges surged to $112.2 million, or 60 cents a share, compared with $65.6 million, or 37 cents a share, in the same quarter a year ago.
With a charge of $6.6 million for the acquisition of OnStream Networks Inc. during the quarter, 3Com had net income of $105.6 million, or 56 cents a share.
Net income in last year's second quarter was $16.3 million, or 9 cents a share, with a $69 million charge for the acquisition of Chipcom Corp.
Even with the charge, 3Com beat Wall Street consensus forecast of 55 cents a share, according to analyst research firm First Call.

"They had a terrific quarter," said Eric Blachno, analyst at Bear Stearns in New York. "3Com is the strongest player in the lower end of the market, and we think those markets are growing much faster" than the rest of the industry.
Second-quarter revenue jumped 46 percent to $820.3 million from $563.5 million a year ago, the company said.

3Com makes equipment that handles information flow between computers. The company said it gained market share during the quarter in its areas of expertise, which includes electronic components to tie PCs to networks. Sales of network adapter cards jumped 55 percent to $353.2 million.
Some analysts had been concerned that Intel Corp.'s entry in the PC networking industry would hurt 3Com's business. But Blachno said 3Com was holding its ground.

The company also had strong sales in relatively new product areas. It said sales of switches and hubs -- the devices that serve as the backbone of large corporate networks -- rose 41 percent to $460.7 million in the quarter.
